paras: The police killing of a Black man at City Point, Virginia, took place on the night of August 8, 1915, when a police officer shot dead an unnamed Black man he was trying to arrest. According to the only report, the man resisted arrest and fired at the officer, and an inquest exonerated the officer.

The Richmond Virginian's Petersburg correspondent, writing under an August 9 dateline, reported that "a negro was shot and killed at City Point last night by a police officer." In that account the man "resisted arrest and shot at the officer, who thereupon shot and killed the negro." The item names neither the dead man nor the officer, and it does not say why the arrest was attempted, whether the officer was hit, or who saw the shooting.
An inquest was held over the body, and the officer was exonerated. No report of further proceedings, and no identification of the dead man, appears in the coverage.

The killing reached print as a three-sentence item headed "Negro Shot by Officer" in the Virginian's Petersburg column of August 10, between death notices and after reports of a fugitive's arrest at Hopewell and a Petersburg patrolman wounded by a Black man. The item gave the account that the man resisted and fired first as fact, with no named source, and closed with the officer's exoneration. No other white paper and no Black newspaper is known to have reported the killing.
